## Packages

```{r packages}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)
library(jsonlite)
```

## Overview

This notebook reproduces the logic in `Health_Outcome_Analysis/Coding/Targeted_ExWAS/targeted_exwas_core.py` in R and is set up to run locally in a regular sequential loop rather than through a SLURM array. It:

- reads the harmonized targeted, outcome, and SDOH CSV files
- standardizes `Study` names by stripping suffixes such as `_Targeted`, `_Outcomes`, and `_SDOH`
- removes the targeted markers excluded in the Python workflow
- converts targeted concentrations to `ng/mL`, applies `log1p()`, and pivots to wide study-specific exposure matrices
- builds child and maternal task lists across all study-specific outcomes
- runs one unadjusted and one adjusted model per outcome-exposure pair
- executes matching tasks sequentially on the local machine
- writes per-task result tables into the same `panel=.../study=.../outcome=...` folder structure

```{r helpers}
safe_slug <- function(x) {
  out <- x %>%
    as.character() %>%
    str_replace_all("[^A-Za-z0-9_]+", "_") %>%
    str_replace_all("_+", "_") %>%
    str_replace_all("^_|_$", "")
  ifelse(out == "", "value", out)
}

resolve_path <- function(path, doc_dir = NULL) {
  candidates <- c(
    path,
    if (!is.null(doc_dir)) file.path(doc_dir, path) else NULL,
    if (!is.null(doc_dir)) file.path(doc_dir, "..", path) else NULL,
    if (!is.null(doc_dir)) file.path(doc_dir, "..", "..", path) else NULL,
    file.path(getwd(), path),
    file.path(getwd(), "..", path),
    file.path(getwd(), "..", "..", path)
  )
  candidates <- unique(candidates[!is.na(candidates)])
  for (candidate in candidates) {
    if (file.exists(candidate) || dir.exists(candidate)) {
      return(normalizePath(candidate, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE))
    }
  }
  normalizePath(candidates[[1]], winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
}

current_doc_dir <- function() {
  doc_input <- tryCatch(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), error = function(e) character(0))
  if (length(doc_input) == 0 || !nzchar(doc_input)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  dirname(doc_input)
}

# std_study(), to_ng_per_mL() and standardize_binary_outcome() now live in
# harmonization_helpers.R (added 2026-08-11). The local copies were removed:
#   - to_ng_per_mL passed mg/dL, ug/mL, ng/g, pmol/mL, nM and kg/m3 through
#     UNCONVERTED, silently treating them as ng/mL (5.9% of rows, mis-scaled by
#     10^3-10^6).
#   - standardize_binary_outcome picked the case level alphabetically, which
#     inverted CCREOH's Preterm_Birth relative to CEHC and PARENTs.
# See CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md sections 1.1 and 1.4.
source(resolve_path("Coding/Paper1_Submission2/harmonization_helpers.R",
                    doc_dir = current_doc_dir()))

coerce_outcome_numeric <- function(y) {
  if (is.numeric(y)) {
    return(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(y)))
  }
  y2 <- trimws(as.character(y))
  bad <- c("", "nan", "na", "n/a", "none", "null", ".", "missing")
  y2[tolower(y2) %in% bad] <- NA_character_
  y2 <- gsub(",", "", y2, fixed = TRUE)
  y2 <- gsub("^[<>]=?\\s*", "", y2)
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(y2))
}

detect_outcome_type <- function(y) {
  y_non_na <- y[!is.na(y)]
  n_unique <- dplyr::n_distinct(y_non_na)
  if (n_unique == 2) {
    return("binary")
  }
  if (n_unique > 2) {
    return("continuous")
  }
  stop(sprintf("Outcome has %s unique non-missing value(s); cannot model.", n_unique))
}

# standardize_binary_outcome() moved to harmonization_helpers.R (sourced above).

split_by_study_drop_na <- function(df, study_col = "Study", pid_col) {
  studies <- sort(unique(df[[study_col]]))
  out <- vector("list", length(studies))
  names(out) <- studies

  for (study in studies) {
    group <- df[df[[study_col]] == study, , drop = FALSE]
    keep <- colSums(!is.na(group)) > 0
    group <- group[, keep, drop = FALSE]
    if (pid_col %in% names(df) && !(pid_col %in% names(group))) {
      group[[pid_col]] <- df[df[[study_col]] == study, pid_col, drop = TRUE]
    }
    out[[study]] <- tibble::as_tibble(group)
  }

  out
}

dict_wide_by_study <- function(
  df,
  pid_col,
  analyte_col = "Analyte_Code",
  value_col = "Concentration",
  units_col = NULL,
  study_col = "Study",
  transform = "log1p"
) {
  d <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[study_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[pid_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[analyte_col]])
    ) %>%
    mutate("{value_col}" := suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[value_col]])))

  if (!is.null(units_col) && units_col %in% names(d)) {
    d[[value_col]] <- to_ng_per_mL(d[[value_col]], d[[units_col]])
  }

  if (transform == "log1p") {
    values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d[[value_col]]))
    d[[value_col]] <- NA_real_
    valid_mask <- !is.na(values) & values >= 0
    d[[value_col]][valid_mask] <- log1p(values[valid_mask])
  }

  out <- list()
  for (study in sort(unique(d[[study_col]]))) {
    group <- d %>% filter(.data[[study_col]] == study)

    if (transform == "percentile") {
      group <- group %>%
        group_by(.data[[analyte_col]]) %>%
        mutate(
          "{value_col}" := {
            v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[value_col]]))
            valid <- !is.na(v) & v >= 0
            result <- rep(NA_real_, length(v))
            result[valid] <- dplyr::percent_rank(v[valid]) * 100
            result
          }
        ) %>%
        ungroup()
    }

    wide <- group %>%
      group_by(.data[[pid_col]], .data[[analyte_col]]) %>%
      summarise("{value_col}" := mean(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(
        names_from = all_of(analyte_col),
        values_from = all_of(value_col)
      ) %>%
      rename(!!pid_col := 1L) %>%
      mutate(Study = study, .before = 1)

    fixed <- c("Study", pid_col)
    analytes <- sort(setdiff(names(wide), fixed))
    out[[study]] <- wide[, c(fixed, analytes), drop = FALSE]
  }

  out
}

resolve_forced_covariates <- function(requested, available) {
  resolved <- character(0)
  for (feat in requested) {
    if (feat %in% available) {
      resolved <- c(resolved, feat)
    } else {
      resolved <- c(resolved, available[startsWith(available, paste0(feat, "_"))])
    }
  }
  unique(resolved)
}

mcfadden_r2 <- function(y, p_model) {
  eps <- 1e-12
  p_model <- pmin(pmax(as.numeric(p_model), eps), 1 - eps)
  y <- as.integer(y)
  ll_model <- sum(y * log(p_model) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p_model))
  p_null <- min(max(mean(y), eps), 1 - eps)
  ll_null <- sum(y * log(p_null) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p_null))
  if (!is.finite(ll_model) || !is.finite(ll_null) || ll_null == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  1 - (ll_model / ll_null)
}

build_model_frame <- function(analysis_df, outcome, exposure, covariates, outcome_type) {
  cols <- unique(c(outcome, exposure, covariates[covariates %in% names(analysis_df)]))
  d <- analysis_df[, cols, drop = FALSE]
  d[[exposure]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d[[exposure]]))
  if (identical(outcome_type, "continuous")) {
    d[[outcome]] <- coerce_outcome_numeric(d[[outcome]])
  }
  d <- d[stats::complete.cases(d), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) {
    return(list(data = d, predictors = character(0)))
  }

  predictor_df <- d[, unique(c(exposure, covariates[covariates %in% names(d)])), drop = FALSE]
  for (nm in names(predictor_df)) {
    if (nm != exposure && !is.numeric(predictor_df[[nm]]) && !is.integer(predictor_df[[nm]])) {
      predictor_df[[nm]] <- as.factor(predictor_df[[nm]])
    }
  }

  keep_cols <- vapply(
    names(predictor_df),
    function(nm) {
      if (nm == exposure) {
        return(TRUE)
      }
      dplyr::n_distinct(predictor_df[[nm]], na.rm = TRUE) > 1
    },
    logical(1)
  )
  predictor_df <- predictor_df[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]

  list(data = bind_cols(d[outcome], predictor_df), predictors = names(predictor_df))
}

fit_linear_with_inference <- function(X, y) {
  n <- nrow(X)
  p <- ncol(X)
  if (n <= p) {
    stop("Too few rows relative to predictors.")
  }

  fit <- lm.fit(x = X, y = y)
  beta <- fit$coefficients
  if (fit$rank < p || anyNA(beta)) {
    stop("Design matrix is rank deficient.")
  }

  resid <- y - drop(X %*% beta)
  rss <- sum(resid^2)
  tss <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)
  sigma2 <- rss / (n - p)
  xtx_inv <- solve(crossprod(X))
  se <- sqrt(diag(sigma2 * xtx_inv))
  t_stat <- beta / se
  p_value <- 2 * stats::pt(abs(t_stat), df = n - p, lower.tail = FALSE)
  t_crit <- stats::qt(0.975, df = n - p)
  ci_low <- beta - t_crit * se
  ci_high <- beta + t_crit * se
  r2 <- if (tss > 0) 1 - (rss / tss) else NA_real_
  adj_r2 <- if (is.finite(r2)) 1 - (1 - r2) * ((n - 1) / (n - p)) else NA_real_
  fitted <- drop(X %*% beta)

  list(
    beta = beta,
    se = se,
    p_value = p_value,
    ci_low = ci_low,
    ci_high = ci_high,
    r2 = r2,
    adj_r2 = adj_r2,
    fitted = fitted
  )
}

fit_logistic_with_inference <- function(X, y) {
  n <- nrow(X)
  p <- ncol(X)
  if (n <= p) {
    stop("Too few rows relative to predictors.")
  }

  nll <- function(beta) {
    eta <- drop(X %*% beta)
    sum(log1p(exp(eta)) - y * eta)
  }

  grad <- function(beta) {
    eta <- drop(X %*% beta)
    p_hat <- plogis(eta)
    as.vector(crossprod(X, p_hat - y))
  }

  opt <- optim(
    par = rep(0, p),
    fn = nll,
    gr = grad,
    method = "BFGS",
    hessian = FALSE
  )
  if (opt$convergence != 0) {
    stop(opt$message %||% "optim() failed.")
  }

  beta <- opt$par
  eta <- drop(X %*% beta)
  p_hat <- plogis(eta)
  w <- pmax(p_hat * (1 - p_hat), 1e-8)
  xtwx <- crossprod(X, X * w)
  cov_mat <- solve(xtwx)
  se <- sqrt(diag(cov_mat))
  z_stat <- beta / se
  p_value <- 2 * stats::pnorm(abs(z_stat), lower.tail = FALSE)
  z_crit <- stats::qnorm(0.975)
  ci_low <- beta - z_crit * se
  ci_high <- beta + z_crit * se

  list(
    beta = beta,
    se = se,
    p_value = p_value,
    ci_low = ci_low,
    ci_high = ci_high,
    p_hat = p_hat,
    mcfadden_r2 = mcfadden_r2(y = y, p_model = p_hat)
  )
}

`%||%` <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0 || identical(x, "")) y else x
}

fit_single_model <- function(
  analysis_df,
  panel,
  study,
  outcome,
  exposure,
  covariates,
  model_label,
  outcome_type
) {
  built <- build_model_frame(
    analysis_df = analysis_df,
    outcome = outcome,
    exposure = exposure,
    covariates = covariates,
    outcome_type = outcome_type
  )
  model_df <- built$data
  predictor_cols <- built$predictors
  n <- nrow(model_df)

  if (n < 20) {
    return(tibble(
      panel = panel,
      study = study,
      outcome = outcome,
      exposure = exposure,
      model = model_label,
      status = "skipped",
      error = "Too few complete-case rows.",
      outcome_type = outcome_type,
      model_n = n,
      model_covars = paste(covariates, collapse = ";")
    ))
  }

  if (!(exposure %in% predictor_cols)) {
    return(tibble(
      panel = panel,
      study = study,
      outcome = outcome,
      exposure = exposure,
      model = model_label,
      status = "failed",
      error = "Exposure column missing after encoding.",
      outcome_type = outcome_type,
      model_n = n,
      model_covars = paste(covariates, collapse = ";")
    ))
  }

  exposure_sd <- stats::sd(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(model_df[[exposure]])), na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(exposure_sd) || exposure_sd == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      panel = panel,
      study = study,
      outcome = outcome,
      exposure = exposure,
      model = model_label,
      status = "skipped",
      error = "Exposure has no variation after filtering.",
      outcome_type = outcome_type,
      model_n = n,
      model_covars = paste(covariates, collapse = ";")
    ))
  }

  X_pred <- model_df[, predictor_cols, drop = FALSE]
  for (nm in names(X_pred)) {
    if (nm != exposure && !is.numeric(X_pred[[nm]]) && !is.integer(X_pred[[nm]])) {
      X_pred[[nm]] <- as.factor(X_pred[[nm]])
    }
  }
  X <- stats::model.matrix(~ ., data = X_pred)
  coef_index <- which(colnames(X) == exposure)

  tryCatch({
    if (identical(outcome_type, "continuous")) {
      y <- as.numeric(model_df[[outcome]])
      fit <- fit_linear_with_inference(X = X, y = y)
      return(tibble(
        panel = panel,
        study = study,
        outcome = outcome,
        exposure = exposure,
        variable = exposure,
        model = model_label,
        status = "ok",
        error = "",
        outcome_type = outcome_type,
        model_type = "linear",
        model_n = n,
        n_predictors = length(predictor_cols),
        estimate = unname(fit$beta[coef_index]),
        beta = unname(fit$beta[coef_index]),
        # se recorded directly (added 2026-08-11). It was previously computed
        # here and discarded, forcing downstream meta-analysis to reconstruct it
        # as (ci_high - ci_low)/3.92 -- but these CIs use qt(0.975, n-p), not
        # 1.96, so the reconstruction overestimated se by ~6% at df=20 and
        # biased every rma() fit and every z = beta/se in Figure 3 Panel A.
        se = unname(fit$se[coef_index]),
        df_resid = nrow(X) - ncol(X),
        or = NA_real_,
        ci_low = unname(fit$ci_low[coef_index]),
        ci_high = unname(fit$ci_high[coef_index]),
        p_value = unname(fit$p_value[coef_index]),
        r2 = fit$adj_r2,
        R2 = fit$adj_r2,
        mcfadden_r2 = NA_real_,
        McFadden_R2 = NA_real_,
        predicted_mean = mean(fit$fitted, na.rm = TRUE),
        predicted_sd = stats::sd(fit$fitted, na.rm = TRUE),
        predicted_min = min(fit$fitted, na.rm = TRUE),
        predicted_max = max(fit$fitted, na.rm = TRUE),
        prediction_scale = "fitted_outcome",
        n_case = NA_real_,
        n_control = NA_real_,
        model_covars = paste(covariates, collapse = ";")
      ))
    }

    y <- standardize_binary_outcome(model_df[[outcome]], name = outcome)
    n_case <- sum(y)
    n_control <- length(y) - n_case
    if (n_case < 5 || n_control < 5) {
      return(tibble(
        panel = panel,
        study = study,
        outcome = outcome,
        exposure = exposure,
        model = model_label,
        status = "skipped",
        error = "Too few cases/controls after filtering.",
        outcome_type = outcome_type,
        model_type = "logistic",
        model_n = n,
        n_case = n_case,
        n_control = n_control,
        model_covars = paste(covariates, collapse = ";")
      ))
    }

    fit <- fit_logistic_with_inference(X = X, y = y)
    beta <- unname(fit$beta[coef_index])
    ci_low <- unname(fit$ci_low[coef_index])
    ci_high <- unname(fit$ci_high[coef_index])

    tibble(
      panel = panel,
      study = study,
      outcome = outcome,
      exposure = exposure,
      variable = exposure,
      model = model_label,
      status = "ok",
      error = "",
      outcome_type = outcome_type,
      model_type = "logistic",
      model_n = n,
      n_predictors = length(predictor_cols),
      estimate = beta,
      beta = beta,
      # se is on the LOG-ODDS scale (matches `beta`), while ci_low/ci_high below
      # are exponentiated to the OR scale. Added 2026-08-11; see the linear branch.
      se = unname(fit$se[coef_index]),
      df_resid = NA_real_,
      or = exp(beta),
      ci_low = exp(ci_low),
      ci_high = exp(ci_high),
      p_value = unname(fit$p_value[coef_index]),
      r2 = NA_real_,
      R2 = NA_real_,
      mcfadden_r2 = fit$mcfadden_r2,
      McFadden_R2 = fit$mcfadden_r2,
      predicted_mean = mean(fit$p_hat, na.rm = TRUE),
      predicted_sd = stats::sd(fit$p_hat, na.rm = TRUE),
      predicted_min = min(fit$p_hat, na.rm = TRUE),
      predicted_max = max(fit$p_hat, na.rm = TRUE),
      prediction_scale = "predicted_probability",
      n_case = n_case,
      n_control = n_control,
      model_covars = paste(covariates, collapse = ";")
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    tibble(
      panel = panel,
      study = study,
      outcome = outcome,
      exposure = exposure,
      variable = exposure,
      model = model_label,
      status = "failed",
      error = conditionMessage(e),
      outcome_type = outcome_type,
      model_type = ifelse(identical(outcome_type, "continuous"), "linear", "logistic"),
      model_n = n,
      n_predictors = length(predictor_cols),
      R2 = NA_real_,
      McFadden_R2 = NA_real_,
      predicted_mean = NA_real_,
      predicted_sd = NA_real_,
      predicted_min = NA_real_,
      predicted_max = NA_real_,
      prediction_scale = ifelse(identical(outcome_type, "continuous"), "fitted_outcome", "predicted_probability"),
      model_covars = paste(covariates, collapse = ";")
    )
  })
}

run_one_exposure <- function(
  analysis_df,
  panel,
  study,
  outcome,
  exposure,
  forced_covariates,
  outcome_type
) {
  bind_rows(
    fit_single_model(
      analysis_df = analysis_df,
      panel = panel,
      study = study,
      outcome = outcome,
      exposure = exposure,
      covariates = character(0),
      model_label = "Unadjusted",
      outcome_type = outcome_type
    ),
    fit_single_model(
      analysis_df = analysis_df,
      panel = panel,
      study = study,
      outcome = outcome,
      exposure = exposure,
      covariates = forced_covariates,
      model_label = "Adjusted",
      outcome_type = outcome_type
    )
  )
}

save_results <- function(results, out_dir) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  manifest <- list(tables = names(results), metadata = list())

  has_arrow <- requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)
  manifest$format <- if (has_arrow) "parquet" else "csv"

  for (nm in names(results)) {
    if (has_arrow) {
      arrow::write_parquet(results[[nm]], file.path(out_dir, paste0(nm, ".parquet")))
    } else {
      readr::write_csv(results[[nm]], file.path(out_dir, paste0(nm, ".csv")))
    }
  }

  writeLines(
    jsonlite::toJSON(manifest, pretty = TRUE, auto_unbox = TRUE),
    con = file.path(out_dir, "MANIFEST.json")
  )
}

read_result_table <- function(path) {
  if (grepl("\\.parquet$", path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    if (!requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop("The 'arrow' package is required to read parquet outputs.")
    }
    return(arrow::read_parquet(path) %>% tibble::as_tibble())
  }
  if (grepl("\\.csv$", path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    return(readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE))
  }
  stop(sprintf("Unsupported result file type: %s", path))
}

collect_exwas_results <- function(out_root) {
  out_root <- resolve_path(out_root, doc_dir = current_doc_dir())
  if (!dir.exists(out_root)) {
    stop(sprintf("Output directory does not exist: %s", out_root))
  }

  result_paths <- list.files(
    out_root,
    pattern = "^(summary_table|exposure_results_table|forced_covariates_used_table)\\.(parquet|csv)$",
    recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
  )

  if (length(result_paths) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("No result tables found under: %s", out_root))
  }

  # STALE-RUN GUARDS (2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 3.6).
  #
  # This function globs the output tree recursively with no run identifier, so
  # results from a previous run silently accumulate alongside the current one.
  # That has already happened once: a legacy layout without scale= coexisted here
  # and the figure scripts double-counted it. Two guards:
  #
  # (1) Only accept the current layout (panel=/study=/outcome=/scale=). Anything
  #     else is a leftover from an older run.
  current_layout <- grepl("scale=", result_paths, fixed = TRUE)
  if (any(!current_layout)) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "collect_exwas_results(): ignoring %d result file(s) not in the current panel=/study=/outcome=/scale= layout. Delete the output tree and re-run to clear them.",
      sum(!current_layout)), call. = FALSE)
    result_paths <- result_paths[current_layout]
  }

  # (2) save_results() writes parquet when arrow is available and csv otherwise.
  #     A tree that has seen both formats holds two copies of the same table and
  #     would be read twice. Keep parquet where both exist.
  key <- sub("\\.(parquet|csv)$", "", result_paths)
  dup_key <- key %in% key[duplicated(key)]
  if (any(dup_key)) {
    drop_csv <- dup_key & grepl("\\.csv$", result_paths)
    warning(sprintf(
      "collect_exwas_results(): %d table(s) exist as BOTH .parquet and .csv (a format switch between runs). Using the .parquet copy; delete the tree and re-run for a clean state.",
      sum(drop_csv)), call. = FALSE)
    result_paths <- result_paths[!drop_csv]
  }

  if (length(result_paths) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("No result tables in the current layout under: %s", out_root))
  }

  result_index <- tibble::tibble(path = result_paths) %>%
    mutate(
      file_name = basename(path),
      table_name = sub("\\.(parquet|csv)$", "", file_name),
      rel_path = dirname(path) %>% sub(paste0("^", out_root, "/?"), "", .),
      panel = str_match(rel_path, "panel=([^/]+)")[, 2],
      study = str_match(rel_path, "study=([^/]+)")[, 2],
      outcome = str_match(rel_path, "outcome=([^/]+)")[, 2],
      scale = str_match(rel_path, "scale=([^/]+)")[, 2]
    )

  tables <- split(result_index, result_index$table_name) %>%
    purrr::imap(function(df, nm) {
      purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) {
        src <- df[i, , drop = FALSE]
        tbl <- read_result_table(src$path[[1]])

        if (!("panel" %in% names(tbl))) {
          tbl$panel <- src$panel[[1]]
        }
        if (!("study" %in% names(tbl))) {
          tbl$study <- src$study[[1]]
        }
        if (!("outcome" %in% names(tbl))) {
          tbl$outcome <- src$outcome[[1]]
        }
        if (!("scale" %in% names(tbl))) {
          tbl$scale <- src$scale[[1]]
        }
        tbl$source_file <- src$path[[1]]
        tbl
      })
    })

  list(
    summary_table = tables[["summary_table"]] %||% tibble::tibble(),
    exposure_results_table = tables[["exposure_results_table"]] %||% tibble::tibble(),
    forced_covariates_used_table = tables[["forced_covariates_used_table"]] %||% tibble::tibble()
  )
}

failed_result <- function(task, error) {
  list(
    summary_table = tibble(
      panel = task$panel,
      study = task$study,
      outcome = task$outcome,
      scale = task$scale,
      status = "failed",
      outcome_type = NA_character_,
      n_exposures_tested = 0L,
      n_result_rows = 0L,
      n_ok = 0L,
      n_skipped = 0L,
      n_failed = 0L,
      forced_covariates_used = "[]",
      error = error
    ),
    exposure_results_table = tibble(),
    forced_covariates_used_table = tibble(
      panel = character(),
      study = character(),
      outcome = character(),
      forced_covariate = character()
    )
  )
}

build_shared_pairs <- function(prepared) {
  all_pairs <- list()

  for (panel in c("child", "mat")) {
    panel_data <- prepared[[panel]]
    id_col <- panel_data$id_col
    exposures_by_study <- panel_data$exposures_by_study$log1p
    outcomes_by_study <- panel_data$outcomes_by_study
    sdoh_by_study <- panel_data$sdoh_by_study

    ok_studies <- Reduce(
      intersect,
      list(
        names(exposures_by_study),
        names(outcomes_by_study),
        names(sdoh_by_study)
      )
    )

    for (study in ok_studies) {
      outcomes_df <- outcomes_by_study[[study]]
      exposures_df <- exposures_by_study[[study]]

      outcome_cols <- names(outcomes_df)[
        !(names(outcomes_df) %in% c("Study", id_col, "Child_PID", "Mat_PID")) &
          vapply(outcomes_df, function(x) any(!is.na(x)), logical(1))
      ]
      exposure_cols <- setdiff(names(exposures_df), c("Study", id_col))

      if (length(outcome_cols) == 0 || length(exposure_cols) == 0) next

      merged <- inner_join(
        exposures_df[, c(id_col, exposure_cols), drop = FALSE],
        outcomes_df[, c(id_col, outcome_cols), drop = FALSE],
        by = id_col
      )
      if (nrow(merged) == 0) next

      exp_non_na <- !is.na(as.matrix(merged[, exposure_cols, drop = FALSE]))
      out_non_na <- !is.na(as.matrix(merged[, outcome_cols, drop = FALSE]))

      co_occur <- t(out_non_na) %*% exp_non_na  # n_outcomes x n_exposures

      hits <- which(co_occur > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
      if (nrow(hits) == 0) next

      all_pairs[[length(all_pairs) + 1]] <- tibble(
        panel    = panel,
        study    = study,
        outcome  = outcome_cols[hits[, 1]],
        exposure = exposure_cols[hits[, 2]]
      )
    }
  }

  if (length(all_pairs) == 0) {
    return(tibble(panel = character(), outcome = character(), exposure = character()))
  }

  bind_rows(all_pairs) %>%
    group_by(panel, outcome, exposure) %>%
    summarise(n_studies = n_distinct(study), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_studies >= 2) %>%
    select(panel, outcome, exposure)
}

prepare_inputs <- function(project_root) {
  doc_dir <- current_doc_dir()
  project_root <- resolve_path(project_root, doc_dir = doc_dir)
  input_dir <- file.path(project_root, "Input")

  sdoh <- readr::read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "Harmonized_SDOH.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  outcomes <- readr::read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "Harmonized_Outcomes.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  targeted <- readr::read_csv(
    file.path(input_dir, "Harmonized_Targeted.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    locale = readr::locale(encoding = "latin1")
  )

  sdoh$Study <- std_study(sdoh$Study)
  outcomes$Study <- std_study(outcomes$Study)
  targeted$Study <- std_study(targeted$Study)

  targeted <- targeted %>%
    filter(!(Analyte_Code %in% IL_MARKERS))

  unit_col <- c("Concentration_Units", "Concentration_Unit", "Units", "Unit") %>%
    keep(~ .x %in% names(targeted)) %>%
    first()

  sdoh_keep <- c(
    "Study", "Child_PID", "Mat_PID",
    FORCED_SDOH_CANDIDATES[FORCED_SDOH_CANDIDATES != "Sample_Collection_Year"]
  )
  sdoh <- sdoh[, intersect(sdoh_keep, names(sdoh)), drop = FALSE]

  # ROW MULTIPLICATION FIX (2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 1.3).
  #
  # These two tables were built with distinct(PID, Sample_Collection_Year), which
  # keeps ONE ROW PER (PID, year) rather than one row per PID. 2,355 of 8,801
  # Child_PIDs and 1,569 Mat_PIDs carry more than one collection year (a
  # participant sampled across visits, or analytes run in different years), so
  # the left_join below was many-to-many and inflated the child SDOH table from
  # 11,259 to 17,881 rows -- +58.8% overall, +305% for GOALS.
  #
  # Every duplicated participant then entered the Adjusted models 2-4 times:
  # inflated model_n, understated standard errors, anticonservative p-values,
  # and unevenly so across cohorts -- which is precisely the axis Figure 3
  # compares along.
  #
  # Fixed by collapsing to one row per PID with the median year, matching what
  # Targeted_Quantile_Power_Array.R:223-255 already did correctly. Median (not
  # first/min) so the covariate is not sensitive to row order.
  collapse_sample_year <- function(df, id_col) {
    df %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[id_col]])) %>%
      transmute(
        !!id_col := .data[[id_col]],
        Sample_Collection_Year = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Sample_Collection_Year))
      ) %>%
      group_by(.data[[id_col]]) %>%
      summarise(
        Sample_Collection_Year = if (all(is.na(Sample_Collection_Year))) {
          NA_real_
        } else {
          stats::median(Sample_Collection_Year, na.rm = TRUE)
        },
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  }

  child_sample_year <- collapse_sample_year(targeted, "Child_PID")
  mat_sample_year   <- collapse_sample_year(targeted, "Mat_PID")

  stopifnot(
    !any(duplicated(child_sample_year$Child_PID)),
    !any(duplicated(mat_sample_year$Mat_PID))
  )

  # Harmonized_SDOH is not one row per participant -- GOALS is longitudinal and
  # stores one row per visit (272 participants have genuinely conflicting
  # covariate rows, 1,312 of them in GOALS). Left as-is, those participants enter
  # each model several times. Collapsed here to one row each; see
  # dedupe_participant_rows() for the policy and its caveat.
  child_sdoh_pre <- sdoh %>%
    filter(!is.na(Child_PID)) %>%
    dedupe_participant_rows("Child_PID", age_col = "Child_Age", label = "child SDOH")
  child_sdoh <- child_sdoh_pre %>%
    left_join(child_sample_year, by = "Child_PID") %>%
    select(-any_of("Mat_PID"))
  assert_no_row_multiplication(child_sdoh_pre, child_sdoh, "child SDOH x sample-year join")

  mat_sdoh_pre <- sdoh %>%
    filter(!is.na(Mat_PID)) %>%
    dedupe_participant_rows("Mat_PID", age_col = "Mat_Age", label = "maternal SDOH")
  mat_sdoh <- mat_sdoh_pre %>%
    left_join(mat_sample_year, by = "Mat_PID") %>%
    select(-any_of("Child_PID"))
  assert_no_row_multiplication(mat_sdoh_pre, mat_sdoh, "maternal SDOH x sample-year join")

  child_outcomes <- outcomes %>%
    filter(!is.na(Child_PID)) %>%
    select(any_of(c("Study", "Child_PID", "Mat_PID")), everything())

  mat_outcomes <- outcomes %>%
    filter(!is.na(Mat_PID)) %>%
    select(any_of(c("Study", "Mat_PID", "Child_PID")), everything())

  child_exposures <- list(
    log1p      = dict_wide_by_study(targeted, pid_col = "Child_PID", units_col = unit_col, transform = "log1p"),
    percentile = dict_wide_by_study(targeted, pid_col = "Child_PID", units_col = unit_col, transform = "percentile")
  )
  mat_exposures <- list(
    log1p      = dict_wide_by_study(targeted, pid_col = "Mat_PID", units_col = unit_col, transform = "log1p"),
    percentile = dict_wide_by_study(targeted, pid_col = "Mat_PID", units_col = unit_col, transform = "percentile")
  )

  list(
    child = list(
      id_col = "Child_PID",
      outcomes_by_study = split_by_study_drop_na(child_outcomes, pid_col = "Child_PID"),
      sdoh_by_study = split_by_study_drop_na(child_sdoh, pid_col = "Child_PID"),
      exposures_by_study = child_exposures
    ),
    mat = list(
      id_col = "Mat_PID",
      outcomes_by_study = split_by_study_drop_na(mat_outcomes, pid_col = "Mat_PID"),
      sdoh_by_study = split_by_study_drop_na(mat_sdoh, pid_col = "Mat_PID"),
      exposures_by_study = mat_exposures
    )
  )
}

build_tasks <- function(prepared, shared_pairs, panel_filter = NULL, study_filter = NULL) {
  panels <- if (is.null(panel_filter)) c("child", "mat") else panel_filter
  scales <- c("log1p", "percentile")
  tasks <- vector("list", 0)

  for (panel in panels) {
    panel_data <- prepared[[panel]]
    id_col <- panel_data$id_col
    ok_studies <- Reduce(
      intersect,
      list(
        names(panel_data$outcomes_by_study),
        names(panel_data$sdoh_by_study),
        names(panel_data$exposures_by_study$log1p)
      )
    )
    if (!is.null(study_filter)) {
      ok_studies <- intersect(ok_studies, study_filter)
    }

    panel_shared <- shared_pairs %>%
      filter(.data$panel == .env$panel)

    for (study in sort(ok_studies)) {
      outcomes_df <- panel_data$outcomes_by_study[[study]]
      outcome_cols <- names(outcomes_df)[
        !(names(outcomes_df) %in% c("Study", id_col, "Child_PID", "Mat_PID")) &
          vapply(outcomes_df, function(x) any(!is.na(x)), logical(1))
      ]

      for (outcome in outcome_cols) {
        allowed <- panel_shared %>%
          filter(.data$outcome == .env$outcome) %>%
          pull(exposure)

        if (length(allowed) == 0) next

        for (scale in scales) {
          tasks[[length(tasks) + 1]] <- tibble(
            panel = panel,
            study = study,
            outcome = outcome,
            scale = scale,
            id_col = id_col,
            allowed_exposures = list(allowed)
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  bind_rows(tasks)
}

run_task <- function(task, prepared) {
  panel_data <- prepared[[task$panel]]
  outcomes_df <- panel_data$outcomes_by_study[[task$study]]
  exposures_df <- panel_data$exposures_by_study[[task$scale]][[task$study]]
  sdoh_df <- panel_data$sdoh_by_study[[task$study]]
  id_col <- task$id_col

  # OUTCOME-TABLE PSEUDO-REPLICATION (2026-08-11, second instance of audit 1.3).
  #
  # Harmonized_Outcomes is not one row per participant either. DISCOVER repeats
  # each child's Asthma / Severe_Asthma row up to 14 times, TSIC repeats Asthma,
  # ZIP repeats Gest_Age_Birth. Every repeat was multiplying that participant
  # into the analysis frame through the inner_join below -- on top of the
  # covariate-join inflation fixed in prepare_inputs().
  #
  # Checked before collapsing: for every affected study/outcome the repeats are
  # EXACT (identical outcome value), so distinct() is lossless -- zero
  # participants have conflicting outcome values. If that ever stops being true
  # the guard below fires rather than silently picking one.
  y_df <- outcomes_df[, c(id_col, task$outcome), drop = FALSE] %>% dplyr::distinct()
  exposure_cols <- intersect(
    task$allowed_exposures[[1]],
    setdiff(names(exposures_df), c("Study", id_col))
  )
  if (length(exposure_cols) == 0) {
    stop("No targeted exposure columns found for the task.")
  }

  forced_covariates <- resolve_forced_covariates(
    requested = FORCED_SDOH_CANDIDATES,
    available = setdiff(names(sdoh_df), c("Study", id_col))
  )

  s_df <- if (length(forced_covariates) > 0) {
    sdoh_df[, c(id_col, forced_covariates), drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    sdoh_df[, id_col, drop = FALSE]
  }

  # Guard both joins (2026-08-11). The covariate join was the one that actually
  # multiplied rows (fixed in prepare_inputs), but the outcome join has the same
  # exposure: nothing upstream guarantees one outcome row per participant.
  stopifnot(!any(duplicated(exposures_df[[id_col]])))
  if (any(duplicated(y_df[[id_col]]))) {
    stop(sprintf("outcome table for study=%s outcome=%s has %d duplicate %s values; aggregate to one row per participant first.",
                 task$study, task$outcome, sum(duplicated(y_df[[id_col]])), id_col))
  }
  if (any(duplicated(s_df[[id_col]]))) {
    stop(sprintf("covariate table for study=%s has %d duplicate %s values.",
                 task$study, sum(duplicated(s_df[[id_col]])), id_col))
  }

  analysis_df <- exposures_df %>%
    inner_join(y_df, by = id_col) %>%
    left_join(s_df, by = id_col)

  analysis_df <- analysis_df[, colSums(!is.na(analysis_df)) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  exposure_cols <- exposure_cols[exposure_cols %in% names(analysis_df)]
  if (length(exposure_cols) == 0) {
    stop("No targeted exposure columns remain after merging and dropping all-missing columns.")
  }
  outcome_type <- detect_outcome_type(analysis_df[[task$outcome]])

  results_df <- map_dfr(
    exposure_cols,
    ~ run_one_exposure(
      analysis_df = analysis_df,
      panel = task$panel,
      study = task$study,
      outcome = task$outcome,
      exposure = .x,
      forced_covariates = forced_covariates,
      outcome_type = outcome_type
    )
  )

  if (nrow(results_df) == 0) {
    results_df <- tibble(
      panel = character(),
      study = character(),
      outcome = character(),
      exposure = character(),
      variable = character(),
      model = character(),
      status = character(),
      error = character(),
      outcome_type = character(),
      model_type = character(),
      model_n = numeric(),
      n_predictors = numeric(),
      estimate = numeric(),
      beta = numeric(),
      se = numeric(),
      df_resid = numeric(),
      or = numeric(),
      ci_low = numeric(),
      ci_high = numeric(),
      p_value = numeric(),
      r2 = numeric(),
      R2 = numeric(),
      mcfadden_r2 = numeric(),
      McFadden_R2 = numeric(),
      predicted_mean = numeric(),
      predicted_sd = numeric(),
      predicted_min = numeric(),
      predicted_max = numeric(),
      prediction_scale = character(),
      n_case = numeric(),
      n_control = numeric(),
      model_covars = character()
    )
  }

  results_df[["scale"]] <- task$scale

  summary_tbl <- tibble(
    panel = task$panel,
    study = task$study,
    outcome = task$outcome,
    scale = task$scale,
    status = ifelse(any(results_df$status == "ok"), "ok", "failed"),
    outcome_type = outcome_type,
    n_exposures_tested = length(exposure_cols),
    n_result_rows = nrow(results_df),
    n_ok = sum(results_df$status == "ok"),
    n_skipped = sum(results_df$status == "skipped"),
    n_failed = sum(results_df$status == "failed"),
    forced_covariates_used = as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(forced_covariates, auto_unbox = TRUE)),
    error = ""
  )

  cov_tbl <- tibble(
    panel = task$panel,
    study = task$study,
    outcome = task$outcome,
    scale = task$scale,
    forced_covariate = forced_covariates
  )

  if (nrow(cov_tbl) == 0) {
    cov_tbl <- tibble(
      panel = character(),
      study = character(),
      outcome = character(),
      scale = character(),
      forced_covariate = character()
    )
  }

  list(
    summary_table = summary_tbl,
    exposure_results_table = results_df,
    forced_covariates_used_table = cov_tbl
  )
}
```

## Load Inputs And Build Tasks

```{r prepare}
doc_dir <- current_doc_dir()
project_root <- resolve_path(params$project_root, doc_dir = doc_dir)
out_root     <- resolve_path(params$out_root,     doc_dir = doc_dir)

prepared <- prepare_inputs(project_root)
shared_pairs <- build_shared_pairs(prepared)
tasks <- build_tasks(
  prepared = prepared,
  shared_pairs = shared_pairs,
  panel_filter = params$panel,
  study_filter = params$study
)

tasks <- tasks %>%
  mutate(local_task_id = row_number(), .before = 1)

# params$outcome is applied once, in the select-tasks chunk below, as a regex
# pattern. The exact-match filter that used to sit here was redundant with it
# and had different semantics (== vs str_detect), so two different meanings of
# the same parameter coexisted. Removed 2026-08-11.

tasks
```

## Select Tasks To Run

```{r select-tasks}

# Outcome restriction (documented 2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md 3.7).
#
# This filter was previously the bare literal `c("Asthma|BMI|Birth")` applied
# unconditionally, which silently overrode the documented params$outcome
# interface and was invisible to anyone reading the YAML header. Promoted to a
# named parameter with an explicit opt-out.
#
# Note it is a SUBSTRING match, so "Birth" also selects Birth_Order,
# birth_due_date, Low_Birthweight and Birth_Weight_Z. Listed exhaustively below
# rather than relying on the regex so the analysed set is visible.
# EXPANDED 2026-08-11. Was "Asthma|BMI|Birth".
#
# Added the cardiometabolic block, which has real cross-cohort overlap that the
# old filter excluded. Every one of these resolves to the SAME four legacy PFAS
# (PFHXS, PFNA, PFOA, PFOS), because the contributing cohorts are PFAS-focused:
#   GOALS  8 analytes | NASH 7 | SEARCH 4  -> intersection = those four
# so this is coherently "PFAS x cardiometabolic outcomes", not a scattering of pairs.
#
#   Cholesterol_HDL / _LDL / Triglycerides   GOALS, NASH, SEARCH   n ~ 6,330
#   Cholesterol_Total, Glucose, Insulin,
#     Insulin_Resistance, ALT                GOALS, NASH           n ~ 2,750
#   Systolic_BP / Diastolic_BP               GOALS, SEARCH         n ~ 4,560
#
# Coding verified consistent across cohorts (mg/dL scales agree). The GOALS-vs-NASH
# ALT gap (median 22 vs 84) is biological -- NASH is the steatohepatitis cohort --
# not a unit error.
#
# APGAR was considered and REJECTED: ELEMENT codes it on a 1-3 scale rather than
# 0-10, and CCREOH carries 12 non-integer values. Excluding ELEMENT leaves APGAR_1
# with zero usable analytes and APGAR_5 with five at K=2.
OUTCOME_PATTERN <- params$outcome %||% paste(
  "Asthma|BMI|Birth",
  "Cholesterol_HDL|Cholesterol_LDL|Cholesterol_Total|Triglycerides",
  "Glucose|Insulin|Insulin_Resistance|ALT",
  "Systolic_BP|Diastolic_BP",
  sep = "|")

selected_tasks <- if (identical(OUTCOME_PATTERN, "ALL")) {
  tasks
} else {
  tasks %>% filter(str_detect(outcome, OUTCOME_PATTERN))
}

message("Outcome filter: '", OUTCOME_PATTERN, "' selected ",
        n_distinct(selected_tasks$outcome), " distinct outcomes:\n  ",
        paste(sort(unique(selected_tasks$outcome)), collapse = ", "))

if (nrow(selected_tasks) == 0) {
  stop("No tasks matched the selected panel/study/outcome filters.")
}

if (!isTRUE(params$run_all_tasks) && nrow(selected_tasks) > 1) {
  stop(
    paste(
      "More than one task matched your filters.",
      "Narrow params$panel / params$study / params$outcome, or set params$run_all_tasks = TRUE."
    )
  )
}



```

## Run ExWAS

```{r run-exwas}
all_results <- vector("list", nrow(selected_tasks))
names(all_results) <- paste0(
  selected_tasks$panel, "__",
  selected_tasks$study, "__",
  selected_tasks$outcome, "__",
  selected_tasks$scale
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_tasks))) {
  task <- selected_tasks[i, , drop = FALSE]
  message(
    sprintf(
      "[INFO] Running local task %s of %s: panel=%s study=%s outcome=%s",
      i,
      nrow(selected_tasks),
      task$panel,
      task$study,
      task$outcome
    )
  )

  results <- tryCatch(
    run_task(task = task, prepared = prepared),
    error = function(e) failed_result(task = task, error = conditionMessage(e))
  )

  out_dir <- file.path(
    out_root,
    paste0("panel=", safe_slug(task$panel)),
    paste0("study=", safe_slug(task$study)),
    paste0("outcome=", safe_slug(task$outcome)),
    paste0("scale=", safe_slug(task$scale))
  )
  save_results(results, out_dir)

  all_results[[i]] <- list(
    task = task,
    out_dir = out_dir,
    results = results
  )
}
```

```{r combined-exposure-results}
combined_exposure_results <- collected_results$exposure_results_table

# OUTPUT TREE + PATH (fixed 2026-08-10). Two problems with the old line
#   save(combined_exposure_results, file = "../../Output/Paper1_OutputV2/Sample_ExWAS_Output.RData")
#   1. It wrote into Paper1_OutputV2, the PREVIOUS submission's output tree.
#      Retargeted to Paper1_Output_Submission2 together with its only consumer,
#      Vis_Code/Toy_ExWAS_Replication_Vis.Rmd (which now loads the new path).
#   2. The path is relative to THIS document's directory, so it only resolves
#      when the notebook is knitted from Coding/Paper1_Submission2/. Knitting
#      from the project root errored here AFTER all the modelling had finished.
#      Now routed through resolve_path()/out_root like every other output.
sample_out <- file.path(
  resolve_path("Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2", doc_dir = current_doc_dir()),
  "Sample_ExWAS_Output.RData"
)
save(combined_exposure_results, file = sample_out)
cat("Saved combined exposure results to", sample_out, "\n")
```
